name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped

prose.intro_html:
Lasagna has a reputation for being a Sunday project, the kind of dish you only make when you have three hours and nothing better to do. This one throws that reputation out the window. We are stacking frozen breaded chicken bites, a blended cottage cheese and alfredo sauce, and no-boil noodles into a single pan, and every serving lands at 496 calories with 40.7 grams of protein. That is a real dinner that eats like comfort food and prices like a budget line item.

The whole trick here is the cottage cheese. Blend it dead smooth with the alfredo and nobody at the table has any idea it is in there, but it does the heavy lifting on protein without dragging in the fat a jar of straight alfredo would. Fourteen containers out of one bake, and you are set for two solid weeks of dinners that feel like a cheat and cost like a plan.
prose.shop_smart:
The frozen breaded chicken breast bites are the backbone of this build, and you need 2 lb 5 oz of them. Buying them frozen is the whole point: you bake straight from the freezer with no thawing and no babysitting, and the only knife work comes after they leave the oven, when you rough chop them into bite-size pieces.

Cottage cheese is pulling double duty as your protein engine and your sauce base. Get enough for 4 2/3 cups and do not overthink the fat level, because it gets blended completely smooth with 1 3/4 cups of alfredo and the texture out of the tub disappears entirely. Any roasted garlic alfredo works fine here. You are stretching it with cottage cheese anyway, so save the fancy jar for another night.

For the cheese up top, shred the fresh mozzarella off the ball yourself and grate the parmesan off a wedge. Pre-shredded cheese is coated in anti-caking starch that fights the melt and the browning you want on that finished top layer. Round it out with no-boil lasagna sheets so you skip a pot of boiling water, and grab a bunch of fresh parsley for the layers and the garnish.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 425 degrees. Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken bites according to the bag, straight from frozen, then let them cool enough to handle and rough chop them into bite-size pieces. This is the only real prep, and the oven does it while you build everything else.

Blend the cottage cheese, the 1 3/4 cups of alfredo, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper until the mixture is completely smooth. That blend is the sauce for every single layer, so do not rush it. You want no cottage cheese curds left behind, just a silky alfredo.

Now assemble. Coat the bottom of your baking dish with a thin layer of the blended sauce, then lay down three no-boil sheets. Add another layer of sauce, a scatter of chopped chicken, some parsley, then mozzarella and parmesan. Repeat the stack, three sheets at a time, until everything is used, and finish the very top with mozzarella and parmesan only. Keep the parsley to the first two layers so it does not scorch up top.

Cover the dish and bake for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges. Garnish with fresh parsley and a little grated parmesan, then let it rest at least 5 minutes before you slice. That rest is what lets the layers set, so your portions hold their shape instead of sliding apart.
prose.portion_html:
This bakes as one big lasagna and then gets cut into 14 portions, so treat the whole pan as your batch. The clean way to hit 14 even servings is to weigh the finished lasagna, dish and all, then subtract the empty weight of the dish you started with. Divide what is left by 14, and that is your target grams per container.

Cut the pan into a grid that gives you 14 pieces, weigh the first couple against your target, and adjust the cut lines from there. Let it rest before you slice so the layers hold together and each square lifts out clean. Every container lands at 496 calories and 40.7 grams of protein, which is a serious protein number for something that eats like Friday night takeout.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is where it stops being a treat and starts being a strategy. All in, this lasagna lands at ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is 14 full dinners built on a bag of frozen chicken bites, cottage cheese doing the heavy lifting, and one jar of alfredo stretched twice as far as its label ever intended.

Compare that to a single plate of chicken alfredo at any sit-down spot and it is not a close call. You are feeding yourself for two weeks on less than the cost of one night where someone else does the cooking, and you are pulling in 40.7 grams of protein a serving while you do it.

head.description: High-protein chicken alfredo lasagna meal prep with 40.7 grams of protein and 496 calories per serving. Fourteen budget-friendly dinners from one easy bake, with cottage cheese blended into the sauce and no noodle boiling required.

steps: Heat the oven to 425 degrees. Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken bites straight from frozen according to the package, then cool and rough chop them into bite-size pieces.
Blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper until completely smooth to make the sauce for every layer.
Coat the bottom of the baking dish with a thin layer of the blended sauce, then lay down three no-boil lasagna sheets.

Top with more sauce, chopped chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat three sheets at a time until assembled, keeping parsley to the first two layers and finishing the top with only mozzarella and parmesan.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning at the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated parmesan, then let it rest at least 5 minutes before slicing into 14 portions.
